Outcome: Performance of IGRAs against dichotomous measure of exposure
Principal Findings: Pooled Odds ratios • QFT-G/QFT-GIT: OR 1.30 (95% CI 0.20-8.32) • T-SPOT: OR 2.24 (95% CI 0.88-5.64) • TST (10mm): OR 0.81 (95% CI 0.38-1.74)
What do these findings mean?: Children exposed to TB have a higher risk of LTBI, expressed by a higher probability of a positive test for LTBI (QFT, T-SPOT or TST) than in unexposed children. Wide and overlapping confidence intervals indicate similar performance of all three tests.

Outcome: Performance of IGRAs against exposure gradient
Principal Findings: 1. Pooled correlation between test and exposure gradient: • QFT-G/QFT-GIT: 0.28 (95%CI 0.06-0.86, I2 0.90) • T-SPOT (not pooled, 1 study): 0.15 (95% CI 0.02-0.37) • TST (10 mm): 0.22 (95% CI 0.11-0.39, I2 0.65) 2. Regression slopes • QFT-G/QFT-GIT: 1.84 (95%CI 1.38-2.44, I2 0.66) • T-SPOT: 1.63 (95%CI 1.12-2.39) • TST (10 mm): 1.73 (95% CI 1.36-2.20, I2 0.59)
What do these findings mean?: A higher level of exposure to TB indicates a higher risk for LTBI, expressed by a positive correlation between LTBI test and exposure gradients. IGRAs and TST show a similar correlation with exposure gradients (wide and overlapping confidence intervals).
